description:
## Question

The runner from ADR 0001 speaks buck2's test-runner protocol (test.proto and a subset of data.proto, pinned to the exact buck2 version), talks REAPI to the local cache, and replaces the OSS runner. Rust or Go? Weigh: proto and gRPC tooling in each, how the tk/tw Go code and the Rust tools are built and shipped today, whether the OSS runner's code (Rust) or quokka's (Rust) can be reused or ported, and the Buck2 build of the tool itself.

comments.text:
Resolution (grilled 2026-09-25).
1. The runner is written in Rust. Parity with buck2's OSS runner (app/buck2_test_runner, Rust) is the riskiest requirement, and quokka is Rust too. The REAPI side is only FindMissingBlobs, BatchUpdateBlobs and UpdateActionResult via tonic. Coupling to tk (Go) is a runtime signal and config, not shared code. This follows the repo's move to Rust tools (rustdeps-gen, hooks).
2. Protocol code is generated at build time from pinned upstream sources, never hand-copied: buck2's test.proto and data.proto fetched by Nix at the same revision as the pinned buck2 binary (one Nix expression holds the revision, and both read it), and the REAPI protos from bazelbuild/remote-apis at a pinned revision. We reject quokka's hand-copied data.proto subset.
3. A new crate in this repo that reimplements the OSS runner's behaviour, using it as a reference. We don't build or patch upstream's buck2_test_runner crate, because that brings back buck2's internal crates, its nightly toolchain and most of the from-source cost ADR 0001 avoided. A parity test suite runs the same targets under both runners and gates every buck2 bump.

title: Which language is the caching test runner written in?
